title: Timeout Policies
summary: Allocate end-to-end deadlines across queueing, inference, tools, retries, and finalization so work stops predictably and uncertain side effects are reconciled.
overview: Timeout policies bound how long a caller waits for an operation; deadlines express when the overall task must finish. Use both deliberately. A per-call timeout that resets at every layer can exceed the user's total budget, especially when retries, queueing, and nested agent calls accumulate.

Distinguish connection establishment, response headers, idle streaming, and total execution time. A timeout does not prove that the remote operation stopped or failed. For commands, the result may be unknown even after the caller gives up, so preserve operation identity and reconcile before retrying. Cancellation is cooperative unless the remote system offers stronger guarantees.

production.poc: A prototype should set explicit model and tool timeouts and record actual latency distributions. Include slow connections and long silent streams in tests.
production.production: Production propagates a parent deadline, allocates remaining time to each stage, and reserves finalization capacity. Retry decisions must account for whether another attempt can finish usefully before the deadline.
production.scale: At scale, tune by task class and dependency percentiles, including network and queue delay. Watch false timeouts and abandoned downstream work because overly aggressive limits can amplify load through retries.

components.name: Deadline context
components.role: Carries the task's remaining time through workers, tools, and delegated agents.

components.name: Stage budget allocator
components.role: Divides available time among required work, retries, and finalization.

components.name: Timeout adapter
components.role: Applies connection, idle, and total-call limits supported by each client library.

components.name: Cancellation coordinator
components.role: Stops optional work and propagates cooperative cancellation when the task expires.

components.name: Outcome reconciler
components.role: Determines whether timed-out commands actually committed before further action.

flow.title: Set task deadline
flow.description: Derive the allowed completion window from the user-facing service contract.

flow.title: Charge elapsed time
flow.description: Include queue wait, prior stages, and delegation overhead in the remaining budget.

flow.title: Allocate call limit
flow.description: Choose a timeout no longer than the useful remaining task window after reserves.

flow.title: Execute and observe
flow.description: Distinguish connection, idle, and total timeout reasons in telemetry.

flow.title: Handle expiry
flow.description: Stop new work, cancel where supported, and classify commands as uncertain until reconciled.

flow.title: Finalize honestly
flow.description: Return complete, partial, deferred, or failed status with the known operation outcome.

diagrams.title: One deadline across multiple stages
diagrams.code:
flowchart LR
 D["Parent deadline"] --> Q["Queue wait"]
 Q --> R["Remaining-time check"]
 R --> M["Bounded model call"]
 M --> T["Bounded tool call"]
 T --> F["Reserved finalization"]
 R --> X["Deadline exhausted"]
 M --> X
 T --> X
 X --> C["Cancel and reconcile"]
 C --> O["Explicit terminal status"]
diagrams.caption: Every stage consumes the same end-to-end allowance, and timeout recovery distinguishes waiting from actual remote completion.

diagrams.title: Timeout does not cancel a committed command
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant A as Agent
 participant T as Remote command service
 participant R as Reconciler
 A->>T: Command with stable operation key
 T->>T: Commit effect
 Note over A: Caller deadline expires
 A->>R: Record uncertain outcome
 R->>T: Query original operation key
 T-->>R: Confirm committed result
 R-->>A: Update durable operation status
diagrams.caption: The user-visible wait can end before the remote effect is known; reconciliation resolves that uncertainty without duplication.

useCase.title: Handling an uncertain reservation hold
useCase.situation: A corporate travel assistant checks availability and places a temporary reservation hold after user confirmation.
useCase.problem: The booking service can accept a hold while its response is delayed beyond the client timeout.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must respect the interactive deadline without placing duplicate holds or falsely reporting failure.
useCase.architecture: A parent deadline covers search, confirmation, and hold creation; the command uses a stable operation key and reconciliation endpoint.
runtime: The assistant spends part of its budget on availability, then allocates only the remaining safe window to hold creation.
If the call times out, the interface reports a pending outcome while reconciliation checks the original operation key.
useCase.failure: A confirmed existing hold is returned to the user; no new hold is created merely because the first response was late.
useCase.impact: Track timeout reason, false-timeout rate, downstream work after cancellation, and time to reconcile uncertain holds.

tradeoffs.benefit: User waits and occupied resources are bounded.
tradeoffs.cost: Healthy slow requests may be abandoned and retried unnecessarily.

tradeoffs.benefit: Nested work cannot silently exceed the service budget.
tradeoffs.cost: Some stages must skip optional work or return partial results.

tradeoffs.benefit: Operators can distinguish connection and processing problems.
tradeoffs.cost: Client libraries differ in what their settings actually cover.

failures.scenario: A timeout excludes DNS or TLS setup
failures.detection: Observed wall-clock duration exceeds the configured request limit.
failures.recovery: Verify client semantics and apply a true total deadline.

failures.scenario: Each retry receives the original full timeout
failures.detection: Total elapsed time exceeds the parent contract.
failures.recovery: Recompute limits from remaining time before every attempt.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming timeout means no side effect occurred
mistakes.fix: Reconcile commands using stable operation identity.

mistakes.mistake: Ignoring queue delay in the budget
mistakes.fix: Charge time from accepted request to final delivery.

mistakes.mistake: Using one timeout for all task classes
mistakes.fix: Tune against dependency behavior and user expectations.

whenToUse: Requests depend on remote or variable-latency services.
Users need predictable completion or explicit deferred status.
Retries and nested calls could exceed total budgets.
whenNotToUse: The operation is intentionally unbounded with no useful deadline.
A timeout would be interpreted as guaranteed remote cancellation.
The system cannot represent uncertain command outcomes.
